Custom Anchor IDs

An author can name a heading's anchor with the {#custom-id} syntax every other Markdown tool understands, rather than accepting the one Mark derives from the heading text.

custom-idMy Heading

The braces are consumed rather than rendered, so the heading reads as written and the anchor is exactly what was asked for: exact.

Another-HeadingAnother Heading

A heading with no custom id keeps its derived anchor, and a link written in the usual slug style still finds it: slug.

relRelease Notes

Naming an anchor replaces the derived one rather than adding to it, so the slug of the heading text no longer resolves: by slug is left as written, while by name resolves. This is what other Markdown tools do too -- a custom id is the id, not an alias.
